question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Costs an arm and a leg
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Costs an arm and a leg"** means something is very expensive or costs a great deal of money. It implies that the cost is so high that it is as if one had to give up something as valuable as an arm or a leg. (बहुत महंगा)

 
 
• **Example: **Buying a new car nowadays costs an arm and a leg due to the increased prices.
 
 

 
• The correct option, **"To be very expensive"**, directly aligns with the idiom's meaning. It indicates a high cost, often prohibitively so, for a product or service. (बहुत महंगा)

 
 
• **Example: **The designer dress was so beautiful but it was too expensive for me to afford.
 
 

 
• Hence, we can infer that the most appropriate meaning of the idiom "Costs an arm and a leg" is **"To be very expensive"**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To be affordable** (किफायती होना): Something that is reasonably priced and within one's budget.
 
 
• **Example:** I am looking for a smartphone that is both advanced and affordable.
 
 

 
• **To be moderately priced** (मध्यम मूल्य होना): Neither too expensive nor too cheap; reasonably priced.
 
 
• **Example: **The restaurant offers a variety of dishes that are moderately priced.
 
 

 
• **To be free of charge** (निःशुल्क होना): To cost nothing; being available without any payment.
 
 
• **Example:** The museum entrance is free of charge every first Sunday of the month.
